lesson_title: Two Witnesses, One Truth: Reconciling Control Accounts
hook_text: Two records. Two different answers. R510 apart. Somebody is wrong.
clip_script: Month end. Zanele asks her books one question, two ways. The summary line — the control account — answers: your customers owe you nine thousand eight hundred and sixty rand. The pages, added one by one, answer: nine thousand three hundred and fifty. Five hundred and ten rand between two records that are supposed to be twins. Somebody is wrong. First discipline of the detective: do not choose a favourite witness. Each record was built along its own road — the line from monthly totals, the pages from daily entries — and either road can hide a pothole. The case ends with both stories corrected until, independently, they tell the same truth. That meeting point is the only number worth writing down.
visual_style: Split screen: a single glowing ledger line on the left, a stack of personal account pages on the right, a red R510 gap pulsing between them until four patches slide in and both sides click to R9 900.
pacing: Slow reveal of the two figures, quickening through the four findings, landing hard on the meeting point.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and close the case yourself.
